title: Correct answer revealed before prediction lock: 'deceptive random-split headline' verdict shown on Prediction step
devpost_criterion: Education impact / learning effectiveness; core 'sealed prediction' claim
environment: browser, verified sample session session_27c89195 and session_e4c7ea89
prerequisites: Start 'Try verified sample', submit any claim, land on Prediction step before sealing
steps: Open sample lesson, enter any claim, click 'Compare two explanations'
On Prediction step, before 'Seal my prediction', read the evidence cards
Observe 'Cell 3 - output 0: This is the deceptive random-split headline under test. accuracy: 0.985'
Observe 'The fairer test: Keep each customer's rows together, then remove customer ID' displayed pre-seal
expected: No verdict or fix language before the seal; the learner chooses an expectation without being told the headline is deceptive
actual: The UI calls the 0.985 accuracy 'the deceptive random-split headline under test' and describes the fix before the learner seals anything, cueing the 'correct' prediction

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Verdict string visible pre-seal in two independent sessions

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: proof record beliefTest.evidenceRefs[1].relevance = 'This is the deceptive random-split headline under test.'

likely_cause: Evidence-card 'relevance' annotations are authored as post-hoc verdicts and rendered statically regardless of seal state
unverified: Whether the live (uploaded-notebook) path shows the same pre-seal annotations
learner_impact: Hindsight-bias protection of the sealed prediction is defeated; learners can appear calibrated without ever committing to a genuine belief
judge_impact: The signature mechanic ('sealed before result') is demonstrably leaky on screen; undermines the thesis demo
trust_impact: A learning scientist judge will flag that the app grades predictions it itself cued
recommended_correction: Gate all verdict/fix language ('deceptive', 'fairer test' description, directive hints) behind the prediction.committed event; show neutral evidence descriptions pre-seal
smallest_correction: Replace pre-seal relevance string with neutral 'accuracy displayed in notebook (random row split)' until sealed
acceptance_criteria: Pre-seal Prediction DOM contains no verdict terms ('deceptive', 'leak', 'fairer test'); identical screenshot test passes across fresh sessions
regression_test: Black-box: fresh sample session, text-search Prediction step pre-seal for 'deceptive'; assert absent; assert present post-result

title: Both 'competing models' and the learner's own 'explanation' are system-authored; identical paraphrase for different learner claims
user: learner who wrote a custom claim vs learner who used starter claim
devpost_criterion: Education impact; 'elicits the learner's actual belief' claim
prerequisites: Two sample sessions with materially different claims
steps: Session A: write a custom claim; Session B: click 'Use a starter claim'
Advance both to Prediction
Compare 'Your current explanation' text
expected: The operationalized explanation reflects the learner's own words, or the learner is asked to state the model themselves
actual: 'Your current explanation' is byte-identical across different claims ('The notebook's random-row test accuracy demonstrates generalization to new customers.'); proof record shows belief_test.proposed actor=system, learner only confirms; 'Edit my explanation' routes back to the raw claim, the paraphrase is never editable

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Identical paraphrase across two sessions with different claims
evidence.ref: agent5_04 vs agent5_29; session_27c89195 vs session_e4c7ea89

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: events[1] belief_test.proposed actor=system; events[2] belief_test.confirmed actor=learner

likely_cause: Fixed belief-test template per concept (entity_leakage); claim text recorded but not used to instantiate hypotheses
unverified: Whether the live path with arbitrary notebooks generates per-claim hypotheses
learner_impact: The learner's role collapses to confirming the tutor's framing; the 'scientific debugger for MY beliefs' promise is not fulfilled at the belief level
judge_impact: A judge testing two different claims sees identical follow-through, reading as scripted
trust_impact: Claim of learner-centred elicitation is overstated
recommended_correction: Require a learner-authored model statement (empty textarea) before showing the system pair; or visibly derive the paraphrase from claim content and let the learner edit the paraphrase itself
smallest_correction: Relabel 'Your current explanation' as 'One explanation that fits your claim' and add required 1-sentence learner restatement before the seal
acceptance_criteria: Different claims yield visibly different explanation cards, or a mandatory learner-authored explanation field (empty by default) gates the seal
regression_test: Two sessions with claims 'the score is meaningless' vs 'model generalizes perfectly'; assert explanation text differs or learner-field is required and initially empty

title: Transfer timeline marks the keyed-correct answer with x and the wrong answer with check (glyph encodes feature property, reads as answer feedback)
steps: Select 'Known item price' for 'Which feature crosses NOW?' -> timeline shows 'uses available information' with a check glyph
Select 'Centered rolling target' (keyed-correct) -> timeline shows 'reads later outcomes' with an x glyph
expected: Glyphs adjacent to the learner's selection communicate answer correctness (or use neutral property icons that cannot be confused with right/wrong)
actual: The wrong selection renders a green check; the correct selection renders a red x at the moment of selection, inverting conventional quiz feedback semantics

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Both directions observed live

likely_cause: Timeline annotation reuses feature-safety icons (safe=check / leaky=x) in a selection-adjacent position
unverified: Colour perception (red/green) verified only via text + glyph in DOM dump
learner_impact: Learners are visually punished for the correct choice and rewarded for the wrong one; confusion or mislearning at the single assessed moment
judge_impact: Any judge clicking the correct transfer answer sees an x beside it; reads as a bug in the flagship gate
trust_impact: Directly contradicts 'verified' branding at the one place the learner is graded
recommended_correction: Replace check/x property glyphs with neutral labels ('available at prediction time' / 'reads future data') and show right/wrong only after 'Check transfer'
smallest_correction: Swap the two glyphs to neutral text badges without check/x iconography
acceptance_criteria: Selecting the keyed-correct feature never renders x/red adjacent to the selection; selecting the keyed-wrong feature never renders check/green
regression_test: Black-box: select each feature, screenshot timeline annotation, assert no x adjacent to 'Centered rolling target' and no check adjacent to 'Known item price'

title: Confidence is preset (72%), recorded, and never used: no calibration feedback after a wrong high-confidence prediction
prerequisites: Seal any prediction with non-default confidence; reach falsifying result
steps: Observe slider preset at 72%
Change to 85%, seal 'Remain near 98%'
Reach 59.4% result and proof page; search for any use of the 85% value
expected: Confidence is elicited without an anchoring default and revisited after the result (calibration feedback)
actual: Preset 72% anchors the estimate; after the falsification no screen references the sealed confidence; Reasoning Diff omits calibration

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Preset 72% observed; changed to 85% successfully

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: predictionContract.confidence=85 with immutableHash; no calibration field anywhere in proof record

likely_cause: Confidence captured for the contract artifact but no pedagogical consumer implemented
learner_impact: Lost metacognitive lesson: overconfidence is the most transferable takeaway and is silently dropped
judge_impact: Minor; visible to judges who inspect the flow
recommended_correction: Remove the preset (start blank), then show a calibration line post-result ('You sealed 85% confidence; the score fell 39 points') in result and proof
smallest_correction: Add one calibration sentence on the result screen referencing the sealed value
acceptance_criteria: Post-result UI contains the sealed confidence number and a calibration statement; slider has no default
regression_test: Seal at 90%, get falsified, assert '90%' appears on result and proof pages

title: Interpretation and boundary discovery are done for the learner: conclusion and boundary stated verbatim; 'Observe' auto-marks Completed
steps: After result, open Observe tab (already 'Completed' with no learner act)
Open Boundary tab: 'The conclusion changes at the entity boundary. The verified whole-customer run has 0 shared customers; the random-row run has 389.'
Note no prompt ever asks the learner to interpret 59.4% in their own words
expected: The learner states what the result means and where the conclusion changes before (or instead of) the app stating it
actual: All interpretation text is pre-written; the only learner act in the Theater is tab-clicking

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Boundary stated verbatim; Observe auto-Completed

likely_cause: Sample path optimized for deterministic demo; no generative checkpoint implemented between result and rule
unverified: Live path may insert generative steps (could not test)
learner_impact: The core sense-making act (evidence -> conclusion) is watched, not performed; retention and transfer suffer
judge_impact: A pedagogy-savvy judge sees lecture, not inquiry, at the pivotal moment
recommended_correction: Insert a required learner interpretation ('In one sentence: which model survived and how do you know?') before revealing the app's reading; make Observe completion contingent on it
smallest_correction: Add one required empty textarea at Observe; reveal app interpretation after submission
acceptance_criteria: Progress past Observe requires a non-empty learner-authored interpretation entered before the app's conclusion text is visible
regression_test: Attempt to advance with empty interpretation (blocked); submit text, assert app conclusion appears only after

title: Rule builder defaults to the fully-correct clause combination; 'Write freely' is pre-filled with the app's rule; prose ungraded and unremarked
steps: Open Apply tab: all three dropdowns already set to the correct clauses
Switch to 'Write freely': textarea pre-filled with the app's composed rule
Proceed: 'CounterLab does not grade your prose' - no feedback on rule content
expected: The learner constructs the rule (empty defaults, distractor clauses present, or free-write starting blank); the system at least mirrors back the rule later
actual: Zero-construction click-through is the default path; free-write starts from app text; rule content receives no response

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Pre-selected dropdowns; pre-filled free-write

likely_cause: Template-first design; no evaluator for learner prose
learner_impact: Reflection step can be completed without a single generated word; illusion of competence
recommended_correction: Empty defaults with at least one distractor per slot; blank free-write; echo the learner's rule at transfer and proof with a self-rating ('does the forecasting case match your rule?')
smallest_correction: Start free-write empty and remove dropdown defaults
acceptance_criteria: Rule builder loads with no clause pre-selected (or blank free-write); at least one keyed-wrong clause exists per slot
regression_test: Load rule builder, assert select values are empty; assert option count >= 3 per slot

title: Mastery language awarded from one 2-item MC transfer gate, passed on retry after an answer-revealing hint
devpost_criterion: Education impact (education-impact claim lacks credible evidence)
prerequisites: Fail transfer once, then pass; reach proof page
steps: Choose wrong transfer answers -> 'Transfer not yet passed' + hint that restates the answer
Choose keyed answers -> 'You applied the rule correctly'; proof page: 'You can now distinguish...'
expected: Mastery claims gated on multiple tasks / first-attempt success, or scoped to the single task; attempts surfaced
actual: Global-sounding capability claim after one gate; retry count invisible in UI; proof record limitation ('does not prove global learner mastery') is not reflected in learner-facing language

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Failed attempt 1 (transfer.failed 23:05:57), passed attempt 2 (transfer.passed 23:07:21); UI shows only 'Passed'

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: limitations: 'Passing transfer verifies fixed choices for this task; it does not prove global learner mastery.'

likely_cause: Single fixed transfer task + celebratory proof copy written independently of the limitations
learner_impact: Overconfidence in a fragile one-shot skill; no incentive for further practice
judge_impact: Education-track judges probing evidence of learning find one MC gate behind a mastery headline
trust_impact: The app's own limitations contradict its UI headline
recommended_correction: Add a second, structurally different transfer task (e.g., class imbalance or group-leakage variant); gate 'You can now distinguish' on first-attempt passes; show attempt history
smallest_correction: Change headline to 'You applied this rule once - first attempt: no' with a 'try another surface' prompt
acceptance_criteria: Proof page shows attempt count and task-scoped capability language; global mastery phrasing absent unless >=2 distinct tasks passed first-try
regression_test: Complete with a failed first attempt; assert proof page displays the failed attempt and no unqualified mastery claim

title: One-click 'starter claim' lets a learner complete the belief step with zero generated content
steps: Click 'Use a starter claim'
Canned claim 'I think the high score means the model will work for completely new customers.' is inserted; step completable without typing
expected: Starter scaffolds (e.g., sentence frames) that still require learner completion; or template use is flagged in the record
actual: Full canned claim inserted and accepted unchanged; flows into 'Your claim' everywhere with no provenance mark

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Starter claim inserted verbatim (78 chars), accepted

learner_impact: Belief elicitation can be bypassed entirely; downstream 'your belief' artifacts may contain no learner content
recommended_correction: Use sentence frames with blanks instead of complete claims; flag template-assisted claims in UI and proof record
smallest_correction: Require >=1 edit to the starter text before 'Compare two explanations' enables
acceptance_criteria: Unedited starter claim cannot advance; or claim is labeled 'template-assisted' at seal and on proof page
regression_test: Insert starter, click through unchanged, assert blocked or flagged

title: Sample 'experiment' is a fixed recording: Explore tab disabled in sample ('Sample result stays fixed'), no learner-manipulable variable
user: learner wanting to probe the result
steps: Open Explore tab
Read 'Sample result stays fixed for a reproducible lesson'; manipulation reserved for live notebook sessions
expected: At least one bounded manipulation (e.g., toggle identity feature, change split) with recomputed verified output in the sample
actual: The only advertised interactive surface is inert in the sample; the test is 'run' by pressing a button that plays fixed values

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Explore panel text: 'Change the test, then let the kernel recompute it... Sample result stays fixed'

likely_cause: Reproducibility constraint chosen over interactivity for the sample path
unverified: Live-path interactivity (file upload blocked in audit environment)
learner_impact: No experimentation = no inquiry skill practiced; the 'scientific debugger' is a movie in the only path most judges will take
judge_impact: High for a 'debugger' claim: judges cannot debug anything in the sample
recommended_correction: Ship one bounded interactive in the sample (identity on/off toggle recomputed by fixed kernel and re-verified)
smallest_correction: Relabel Explore tab honestly as 'available with your own notebook' and add one precomputed side-by-side comparison the learner can reveal by choice
acceptance_criteria: Sample Explore offers >=1 control whose change produces a different verified metric; or tab is clearly labeled demo-only before opening
regression_test: Toggle identity feature in sample; assert metric changes and carries verification badge

title: Failed-transfer feedback does not identify which sub-answer failed and effectively dictates the correct combination
steps: Fail with both answers wrong
Read feedback: 'Use the NOW line: pick a test where training happens before testing, then remove any feature that reads values to the right of NOW.'
expected: Feedback localizes the error (split vs feature) with a hint that preserves the need to think on retry
actual: Single undifferentiated message that restates the rule so directly the retry is answer-copying; unlimited silent retries

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Feedback text observed after deliberate failure

likely_cause: One static failure message regardless of which invariant failed (evaluator knows: checks[] per invariant)
learner_impact: Retry requires no diagnosis; feedback teaches the answer, not the discrimination
recommended_correction: Emit per-invariant feedback from transferResult.checks (name the failed dimension, withhold the correct option); cap retries before revealing the answer
smallest_correction: Say which question failed without giving its answer
acceptance_criteria: Mixed wrong answers produce feedback naming only the failed dimension; correct option strings absent from failure feedback
regression_test: Fail split only; assert feedback references evaluation design and does not contain 'time-ordered holdout'

title: Learner never performs the repair: patch is system-generated; no guided code action before the certificate
steps: Open Repair
Review pre-made scope lists
Click 'Verify notebook patch' -> done
expected: The learner makes at least one substantive repair decision (choose the grouping column, pick the correct diff among candidates, or order the fix steps)
actual: Repair is fully pre-built; the learner's only act is pressing verify

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Repair preview + verify button; diff generated by system

likely_cause: Repair designed as verified-artifact showcase rather than learning activity
learner_impact: The behavioural core (how to fix a split) is demonstrated, not practiced
recommended_correction: Insert a repair-choice gate (e.g., 'which column defines the entity?' or 'which of three diffs is safe?') verified before the real patch compiles
smallest_correction: Require selecting customer_id as the grouping entity from the schema list before 'Verify notebook patch' enables
acceptance_criteria: Repair cannot complete without a recorded learner repair decision; wrong choices produce corrective feedback
regression_test: Attempt verify without selection (blocked); select wrong entity (feedback); select correct (proceeds)

title: No prior-knowledge scaffolding for non-experts: split, ROC AUC, ablation, entity used without any definition affordance or novice path
prerequisites: Read the lesson as a novice
steps: Search UI for definitions of train/test split, ROC AUC, identity ablation, entity
Check home page for a novice path
expected: Inline definitions at first use and/or a 'new to ML?' scaffolded path
actual: No glossary or definitions anywhere; hints explain why steps exist, not what terms mean; home page targets notebook-owning practitioners

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: No definition affordance found across all six steps and home page

likely_cause: Audience assumed to be DS practitioners; no novice layer built
learner_impact: Non-experts can click through (canned path) but cannot build the concepts the lesson is about
judge_impact: If Devpost claims broad educational impact, the accessibility gap is material
recommended_correction: Add tap-to-define glossary terms at first occurrence and a 60-second 'what is a train/test split?' primer card for self-identified novices
smallest_correction: Glossary tooltips on split/ROC AUC/ablation/entity at first use
acceptance_criteria: Each technical term has a definition affordance at first occurrence; home page exposes a novice path

title: No durable review path: sessions survive only as URLs; no library, no spaced retrieval or revisit prompt
prerequisites: Complete a lesson; return to home page
steps: Complete lesson
Revisit home page
Look for prior sessions or review prompts
expected: A session list, continuation affordance, or scheduled retrieval prompt
actual: URLs restore state (verified) but nothing on the home page acknowledges prior work; one lesson exists; no review design
